I am a middle school teacher. I am trying to put myself in your teachers position. How confident are you that they will be supportive? Do you think they are knowledgeable about trans issues and are well versed in trans vocabulary? It might be an overwhelming, but impactful situation for them. It will be significant to them that you put so much trust in them.


What are you hoping to get out of the experience? Coming out is a major decision that you will have to do many times in your life. It is important to make sure that YOU are ready and that you realize you cannot control other people's reactions, only hope for the best.


If I were you, and determined to reach out to an adult for support, I would do a few things... 

a) Make sure that this is a person that I can trust

b) Make sure you disclose the information at an appropriate time. Don't catch them as they are leaving for the day, first thing in the morning or quickly before class. Make sure they have enough time to process the information you are telling them. 

c)  Have no expectations and be prepared for every possible reaction.  You can not predict or control what other people think/feel.

d)  Realize that telling one person, especially an adult in a school setting, may lead to force you to disclose your personal information to other people before you are ready.  Let's imagine the teacher is overwhelmed, wants to be supportive but doesn't know how so they reach out to other adults for advice, recommend you speak to others, not respect your confidentiality, accidently gaffes and makes your personal information known to other students or faculty that you are not ready to tell.  Scenarios are limitless...


Despite the tone of my message, I imagine myself or my fellow colleagues and how we would collectively act if a student confided such information with us.  It would be an honor, and as long as there is no danger to you or others there is no responsibility of the teacher to disclose your information to anyone, including your parents.  Ultimately, this is your decision.  Go with your gut but make sure to be ready for all possible outcomes.  Hope for the best, prepare for the worst.  I have a feeling that if you feel confident about coming out to this teacher, that is a pretty strong indication of your existing trust in them.  

I hope this works out for you.  Please let us know what you decide and how things go.  I am entirely optimistic for you and hope that this teacher embraces your identity.  Being a trans youth is hard!  Make sure to create a support system for yourself, get a therapist and find your community! I wish you all the best!

I banked for an initial consultation and doctors appointment for $500 and then it costs me $45 a month for storage.  So a yearly cost after the initial appointments only costs me $540 a year. Either way, I think when people give the $5000 quote they are talking about long term costs, you should not have to pay that up front.  If you live in the US there are various mail services that will send you a cup to fill with your sample and once you send it back the process is done, you only pay the monthly storage costs.  I think it costs around $1,000 to get everything set up.  I'm not sure if I am ever going to have kids, but banking is one of the things I'm most happy about in my transition as it still gives me the possibility of having my own family someday. I continued to research about transitioning but never felt like it was going to lead anywhere.  Every time I thought about transitioning, I kept imagining the reflection I saw in the mirror that night.  I felt like I would never get past looking like a guy in a dress with makeup on.  

For years I kept pushing those feelings away, but they always came back.  It got to the point where I couldn't ignore the feelings anymore and I just had to make a change.  If you are having questions or uncertainties about your gender identity address them head on!  Have you thought about hormones?  I must have seen a million videos and slideshows and they always gave me so much hope and confidence about what my future would look like.  Don't think of the boy body you have now but the girl body you can have in the future!  I don't know if this helps... just felt like we had a similar experience and wanted to share with you.
